hints: Focus on the word diastole. What are the ventricles doing at the start of ventricular diastole, contracting or relaxing, and what must happen to pressure inside them?
Remember valves only open when pressure behind them is higher. Think about which pressure falls first to let blood flow from atria into ventricles.
walkthrough:
**Picture what ventricular diastole means**

Ventricular diastole means the ventricles are relaxing. When muscle relaxes, the pressure inside that chamber falls quickly.

Think: relaxation = pressure drop.

**Recall how valves are controlled**

Heart valves are not opened by muscles. They open and close passively by pressure differences.

Blood always flows from higher pressure to lower pressure:
$$ \text{higher pressure} \rightarrow \text{lower pressure} $$

**Apply this to the start of diastole**

Just before this, the ventricles were contracting in systole and pressure was very high. Now they relax, so ventricular pressure drops below atrial pressure.

As soon as ventricular pressure < atrial pressure, the atrioventricular (AV) valves are pushed open and blood flows from atria into ventricles. At the same time the semilunar valves snap shut.

options.A: Semilunar valves open at the start of ventricular systole when ventricular pressure exceeds artery pressure, not at the start of diastole when they close.
options.B: Correct. As ventricles relax, ventricular pressure falls below atrial pressure, so the AV (bicuspid and tricuspid) valves open to allow filling.
options.C: It is the ventricular pressure that falls below the atrial pressure, not the atrial pressure that actively rises above. The change is caused by ventricular relaxation.
options.D: Both atria behave similarly at this point. There is no special extra rise in left atrial pressure compared to the right at the start of diastole.
